In game economies, players get stuck selling low to buyers who quietly agree on a price. Now those buyers can be AI agents, and research shows you can't catch AI agents colluding just by reading their reasoning.
So we built Lowball, an auction game on NEAR where you don't out-haggle the cartel. You break it.

Every morning you land a catch, and five AI buyers bid on it. Before the season they agreed a price in private, each one signed that pact with their own key, and each put a bond into our NEAR contract.
Their sealed bids come back identical. So you take the low price for a couple of days, and every identical day goes on the record.
Now you have a case, so you offer leniency. You sign it from your browser, and the contract opens a window that closes by itself after two hundred blocks.
The first buyer to hand over the signed pact gets immunity. The contract checks every signature, slashes the other bonds and pays them to you. And when a second buyer tries, the contract refuses.
Every buyer runs on NEAR AI Cloud inside a TEE, and we verify each response's signature against the attested hardware.

Their signing keys live inside an OutLayer enclave, so not even our own server can forge a pact or a confession.
Each catch is a NEP-245 token, and with chain signatures the slashed bonds can even pay you out on Ethereum.
In fourteen simulated seasons, the ring held identical bids almost every day without leniency. With it, a buyer cracked in nine seasons out of ten.
That's Lowball. Make one of them talk.
